step1_analysis.description: A differential amplifier with a cascode tail current source and Maneatis symmetric loads (diode-connected PMOS in parallel with a biased PMOS). It is typically used as a tunable delay cell in a Voltage-Controlled Oscillator (VCO) or Phase-Locked Loop (PLL), where the bias voltage VBP controls the effective load resistance and thus the delay.

paper_reference.title: A CMOS 400-Mb/s Serial Link for AS-Memory Systems Using a PWM Scheme

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain = gm1 * (1/gm6 || ro5 || ro6). With VN2=0.9V, Itail ≈ 300uA. gm1 ≈ 900uS, gm6 ≈ 340uS, Rout ≈ 2.9kOhm. Gain = 900u * 2.9k = 2.6 V/V = 8.3 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Gain must be >1 (0 dB) to sustain oscillation in a VCO ring, typically designed around 2-5 V/V for fast switching and wide tuning range.

sky130_expected.calculation: BW = 1 / (2 * pi * Rout * Cload). Rout ≈ 2.9kOhm, Cload ≈ 30fF (parasitics + next stage). BW = 1 / (2 * pi * 2.9k * 30f) ≈ 1.8 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Bandwidth must be significantly higher than the 400 MHz data rate to preserve signal edges and minimize jitter.

Power Consumption.description: DC power dissipation of the delay cell.

sky130_expected.calculation: Power = VDD * Itail. VDD=1.8V, Itail ≈ 300uA. Power = 1.8 * 300u = 0.54 mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: A single delay cell consumes a small fraction of the total 66.5 mW transceiver power.

Propagation Delay.description: Time delay from input crossing 50% to output crossing 50%.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Delay must be a fraction of the 500ps bit period, tunable via VBP to lock the PLL/DLL.

Differential Output Swing.description: Peak-to-peak differential voltage swing during transient operation.

sky130_expected.calculation: With a 0.4Vpp differential input and a gain of ~2.6 at 400MHz, the output swing is roughly 0.4 * 2.6 = 1.04Vpp.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Sufficient swing is required to fully switch the subsequent differential pair in the VCO chain.

step3_testbench.description: Measures DC power, AC gain at multiple frequencies, transient output swing, and propagation delay.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Testbench for Differential Delay Cell
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u
.param W_xm7=5u L_xm7=0.5u
.param W_xm8=5u L_xm8=0.5u

XM1 OUTp INn NTAIL GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 OUTn INp NTAIL GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N1 VN2 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 NTAIL VN1 N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 OUTn VBP VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 OUTn OUTn VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}
XM7 OUTp VBP VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm7} w={W_xm7}
XM8 OUTp OUTp VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm8} w={W_xm8}

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VVN2 VN2 0 0.9
VVN1 VN1 0 1.3
VVBP VBP 0 0.99

VINp INp 0 DC 0.9 AC 0.5 SIN(0.9 0.1 400MEG 0 0)
VINn INn 0 DC 0.9 AC -0.5 SIN(0.9 -0.1 400MEG 0 0)

C1 OUTp 0 10f
C2 OUTn 0 10f

.control
  op
  let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
  print power
  
  ac dec 100 1MEG 10G
  let out_diff = v(OUTp) - v(OUTn)
  let gain_mag = mag(out_diff)
  let gain_db = 20*log10(gain_mag)
  
  meas ac gain_1M find gain_db at=1MEG
  meas ac gain_400M find gain_db at=400MEG
  meas ac gain_1G find gain_db at=1G
  
  tran 10p 10n
  let out_diff_tran = v(OUTp) - v(OUTn)
  meas tran diff_max MAX out_diff_tran
  meas tran diff_min MIN out_diff_tran
  let diff_swing = diff_max - diff_min
  print diff_swing
  
  meas tran delay_rise TRIG v(INp) VAL=0.9 RISE=2 TARG v(OUTn) VAL=0.9 FALL=2
  meas tran delay_fall TRIG v(INp) VAL=0.9 FALL=2 TARG v(OUTn) VAL=0.9 RISE=2
  
  quit
.endc
